gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many hours of calls each pick lasts on a charge: rated talk time with ANC on is 24 h for the Sony WH-1000XM6, 21 h for both Jabra Evolve2 85 and Evolve3 85, and 20 h for the soundcore Space 2 Pro. At 4 h of calls a day that is 6.0, 5.25, 5.25 and 5.0 workdays, so the Jabra Evolve3 85's 55 h headline drops to 38% on calls while the Sony keeps 80%.
standout_why: I compared against SoundGuys' 'best noise canceling headphones for work' page, which ChatGPT cited in all three chats. It gives only music-playback figures (Evolve3 85 '55 h', Sony '30 h', measured 37 h 14 min) and says it has no talk-time spec or meeting-hours calculation. I also tried RTINGS' phone-calls page (also cited), RTINGS' work page, What Hi-Fi's mic page and TechRadar's ANC page, but their article bodies did not load, so their pick lists are unchecked. No battery or talk-time figure appeared in the parts that did load. Our own current page already lists talk time for the Space 2 Pro (20 h) and Evolve2 85 (21–26 h) but not for the Sony, and it has no per-workday figure.
decides: This confirms the Sony WH-1000XM6 as best overall for a call-heavy buyer. It has the lowest music headline here (30 h, against Jabra's 55 h) yet the most talk time (24 h), so it lasts longest in meetings. It also stops battery from being a reason to pay the Evolve3 85's ~$649 MSRP (the figure ChatGPT showed): on calls it matches the Evolve2 85 at 21 h. The $199.99 Space 2 Pro gets within one workday of the Sony (5.0 vs 6.0 days at 4 h/day). The Bose QC Ultra (2nd Gen) cannot be ranked on this, because Bose publishes no talk time.
